entry.label: The Hidden Power of Systems Thinking
entry.description: Ray Ison and Ed Straw's account of systems thinking in governance, focused on institutional obstacles, systemic governing and practical principles for acting amid climate and biodiversity emergencies.
aliases: The Hidden Power of Systems Thinking: Governance in a Climate Emergency
entry.canonical_definition: Ray Ison and Ed Straw's account of systems thinking in governance, focused on institutional obstacles, systemic governing and practical principles for acting amid climate and biodiversity emergencies.

profile.title: The Hidden Power of Systems Thinking
profile.canonical_definition: Ray Ison and Ed Straw's account of systems thinking in governance, focused on institutional obstacles, systemic governing and practical principles for acting amid climate and biodiversity emergencies.
profile.summary: The Hidden Power of Systems Thinking connects systems practice to failures and possibilities of governance under climate and biodiversity emergency.
profile.why_it_matters: It moves systems thinking from diagnosis of complex problems to the design of governing relationships, institutions, constitutional arrangements and learning capacity.
common_misreadings: systems thinking itself supplies political legitimacy
governance can be redesigned from one centre
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional and publisher sources. Open to correction, rival interpretation and stronger evidence.
